The dominant signal across two independent paradigms is arachidonic acid metabolism. RaMP ORA returned WP:WP167 'Eicosanoid synthesis' at rank 0 with FDR 3.16e-13 and fold enrichment 1250.95, hitting 5 of 8 inputs (15-deoxy-Δ¹²,¹⁴-PGJ2, arachidonic acid, 5-HETE, 15-HETE, leukotriene A4). Mummichog m/z-direct analysis independently returned 'Arachidonic acid metabolism' as its top hit (p=0.0015, overlap=11 of 11 metabolites) and 'Leukotriene metabolism' as rank 3 (p=0.036). The cross-paradigm winner is therefore arachidonic acid as the pathway hub, with 15-deoxy-Δ¹²,¹⁴-PGJ2 (C14717) as the canonical driver effector — it is the dehydration cyclisation product of PGD2 and a high-affinity PPARγ ligand with documented anti-inflammatory transcriptional activity. 5-HETE and 15-HETE mark concurrent 5-LOX and 15-LOX branch activation.
